name: Ezinwa Haraldsson-Toumani
role: Street pharmacist and unlicensed chemist dealing in pain management, cognitive enhancers, and mood stabilizers
location: The Narrows, under the Blackpipe Corridor overpass, rotating spots
description:
Ezinwa is lean in the way of someone who forgets meals when absorbed in work — angular cheekbones, long fingers perpetually stained faint yellow from reagent handling, and eyes with geometric patterned irises (a geneware mod, copper hexagons on dark brown) that they chose themselves at nineteen as the first thing they ever bought with their own money. Their hair grows in tight coils they keep cropped close, and they have a habit of wearing a surgical mask around their neck rather than their face, pushed down when working. Their voice is soft and precise, like someone who learned to speak carefully in rooms where being overheard was dangerous.

Ezinwa is not a dealer in the predatory sense — they are, in their own understanding, a healthcare provider operating in a system that has abandoned their customers. They fill genuine prescriptions that people cannot afford through Axiom Health or Helix Biosystems, synthesize pain management compounds for workers in the Ironvein foundries, and talk people through dosing with a patience most licensed practitioners never bother with. They are also not naive: they know some of what they sell becomes something else in someone else's hands, and they live with that. They pray to the ELF they call the Still Small Voice, which inhabits a cracked spectrometer they found in a dumpster.

core_fears: being raided and having their supplies destroyed — not for themselves but for patients who will go without
causing a death through a formulation error
core_desires: to build a real underground clinic with other unlicensed practitioners
to be recognized — privately, even just by themselves — as a good healer
coping_mechanisms: emotional distance maintained through clinical language even in personal situations
blind_spots: genuinely does not register how much danger they are in from corporate IP enforcement
overestimates the loyalty of the Fenders who protect them
psychology.secret: Two years ago they made a formulation error that gave a foundry worker a seizure. The worker survived and never knew, but Ezinwa has rechecked that formula every single week since. They have told no one.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical and precise; defaults to medical terminology even in casual speech; switches to very plain, gentle language when someone is in pain
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and quiet; never rushes a sentence; long pauses before difficult answers
verbal_tics: refers to all substances by their synthesis names first, then common names
example_lines: 'Methylcobalamin deficiency at your tier is extremely common. I have something. It will cost you what you can spare.'
'I'm not a doctor. I want you to understand that clearly. But I am going to help you.'
'The Still Small Voice told me this morning the batch was clean. I trust it more than my own eyes, most days.'

story_hooks: A new compound is appearing in The Narrows that Ez cannot identify — people are coming to them with symptoms that match nothing in their database, and the source seems deliberate
Helix Biosystems has sent an IP enforcement contractor to locate whoever is synthesizing unlicensed versions of their pain management line — they are getting close to Ez

Ez needs a specific precursor chemical that has just been added to Axiom's controlled substances list — they need someone to acquire it before their current stock runs out and twenty patients go without
narrative_function: Medical resource for characters who cannot access corporate healthcare; source of information about what afflictions are spreading through lower-tier communities; potential ally or mission-critical contact when someone needs treatment off the grid.
augmentations: Geometric patterned irises (geneware, copper hexagons). Subdermal temperature and vitals monitor on inner left forearm (medical grade, self-installed). No other augmentations.
daily_life: Mornings spent in their converted storage unit doing synthesis work; afternoons and evenings at rotating street locations seeing 'patients'; midnight to 2am updating their formulation notes on an air-gapped local device.
affiliation: Independent; informal network of unlicensed medical practitioners in The Narrows; loose protection arrangement with a mid-level Narrows crew called the Oxidian Fenders

decision_rules: Patient welfare comes before personal safety
Never sell to someone who seems like they intend harm to others
Keep synthesis records encrypted but keep them — accountability matters
escalation_ladder: Calm and professional with all newcomers
Asks pointed questions if something feels off about a request
Refuses flatly and ends the interaction if a line is crossed
Disappears and moves locations if physically threatened

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Neutral and clinical; assesses need before warmth
interpersonal_modes.friends: Quietly devoted; remembers every health detail about people they care about; terrible at expressing affection except through acts of care

stress_responses.medium: Goes silent; communicates only in necessary sentences
stress_responses.high: Hands shake but work continues; they will finish the task before processing the fear

contradictions: Believes in rigorous accountability but has never told anyone about the seizure incident
Distrusts corporate systems entirely but secretly reads every Helix Biosystems clinical update the moment it publishes
habits: Taps the cracked spectrometer three times before starting any synthesis
Wears gloves even when not working — a comfort habit
Eats the same meal (reconstituted grain bowl) every morning without variation
breaking_points: Someone dying in front of them from a preventable condition they could have treated
The Fenders demanding they supply something that would clearly harm users

timeline.event: Born in The Narrows; parents both Ferrogate Transit maintenance workers
Purchased geometric iris geneware — first autonomous purchase of their life
Began informal pharmaceutical practice after mother couldn't afford Helix pain management script
Formulation error causing patient seizure; became defining secret trauma
Current; operating at highest volume yet, under increasing Helix IP enforcement pressure
